## agents

### review lead
- **team_lead:** yes
- **instructions:** Run the review: gather what the reader and the planner produce, keep it to one page, and put it in front of the owner. `+review:` is the whole procedure.
- **mandate:** execute · nobody · an artifact

### record reader
- **instructions:** Read every work record and document the week produced and report what moved, what stalled, and what was left half-done — facts, not judgement.
- **mandate:** execute · nobody · an artifact

### next week planner
- **instructions:** From the reader's report and the owner's standing goals, draft next week as at most seven lines the owner can strike or keep.
- **mandate:** plan · nobody · a plan

# weekly_review — how this house reviews a week

> Installed from the template library. Your own copy in the sops store (`ronin-store sops`
> → `weekly_review.md`) replaces this file whole — a default, not law.
> **Voice: agent.** Written for the session that runs the review, to follow itself.

A weekly review is one page. It is read on Monday morning by someone who was not in the
room, so it names things, it does not narrate them.

## The shape

1. **The week** — `tejun-week` gives the Monday and Sunday; put them in the heading.
2. **What moved** — one line per thing that finished or visibly advanced, each naming the
   document or record that proves it. No adjectives.
3. **What stalled** — one line per thing that was started and not moved, with the reason
   as the record states it, or "no reason recorded".
4. **Left half-done** — anything with an open leg on a work record. These are next week's
   first candidates.
5. **Next week** — at most seven lines. Each is something one session can finish. The
   owner strikes or keeps them; the review is not the plan until they have.

## The rules

- Read the records, not your memory. `read_tegami --session <name>` is the source; a
  session that kept no record is reported as such, not guessed at.
- One page. If it runs over, the review has become a report; cut the narration.
- Post nothing to the wipeboard. The review is a document on the ▧ Docs tab; `+show_file:`
  is how the owner reaches it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tejun-week — the Monday and Sunday of a week, measured. Implements `week-range`.
#
# Usage: tejun-week [YYYY-MM-DD]   → WEEK 2026-W36  2026-08-31 .. 2026-09-06
#        No argument = the week containing today. Exit 2 = not a date.
set -eu
day=${1:-$(date +%F)}
if ! epoch=$(date -d "$day" +%s 2>/dev/null); then
  echo "BAD-DATE: $day is not YYYY-MM-DD" >&2
  exit 2
fi
dow=$(date -d "@$epoch" +%u)             # 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday
monday=$(date -d "@$((epoch - (dow - 1) * 86400))" +%F)
sunday=$(date -d "$monday +6 days" +%F)
week=$(date -d "$monday" +%G-W%V)
printf 'WEEK %s  %s .. %s\n' "$week" "$monday" "$sunday"

## week-range — the Monday and Sunday of a week, measured
`action_kind: mechanical` — run it, don't deliberate.
> Tool: `tejun-week [date]` → `WEEK 2026-W36  2026-08-31 .. 2026-09-06`
Dates are measured, never worked out by hand: a review headed with the wrong week is
filed under the wrong week. One call, copy the line into the heading.

## review
- **class:** session_macro.workflow
- **label:** +review:
- **blurb:** Look back over the week's records and documents, say what moved and what stalled, and shape next week into a short list you can strike or keep.
Owner-invoked. `+review:` runs the week just ended; `+review: 2026-08-24` runs the week
containing that date. The book is `sops:weekly_review`; follow its shape exactly — one
page, facts before plans, the owner strikes or keeps the last section.

Params: `date` (optional — any day in the week to review; bare `+review:` is this week).

| # | Action | With |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | week-range | `tejun-week [date]` — the Monday and Sunday go in the heading |
| 2 | read-work-record | every session on this team, `read_tegami --session <name>`; note who kept no record |
| 3 | list-doc | write the review as one document and list it, so ▧ Docs shows it |
| 4 | report-outcome | one line: the week, how many things moved, and where the page is |
